name: inprocess-wbcpu-apb-timer-f1f4
notes: One Wishbone CPU (PicoRV32) and the PULP APB3 timer target on the same fixed RAM image; no DMA model is declared, so F6 is refused by name (unsupported-f6:no-dma-model)

the RAM image starts at 0 because this CPU's own boot contract declares reset_vector 0 (boot_address_required false); the entry takes the boot address from that contract and refuses a RAM image that does not contain it

this CPU declares a 32-bit irq vector rather than a one-bit machine-external input, and no per-bit wiring is declared for it: the host holds the vector at zero and the entry refuses F5 by name (unsupported-f5:cpu-irq-unwired:wishbone:32-bit-irq-held-at-zero).  The timer's four declared F5 facts are present in this declaration and are still not used
the target window is the timer's declared 4 KiB APB window at 0x40000000
the cpu and target declare 50 MHz, so assume_single_clock states that one host tick drives both models
